value.name: 12' · Ademola Lookman v Bayer Leverkusen
value.narrative: Teun Koopmeiners: won the ball and played Zappacosta in. Davide Zappacosta: sent an angled ball back across the box. Ademola Lookman: arrived behind his marker and finished at the far post.

goals.notes: Score is Atalanta's tally first, after the goal. UEFA (official): Koopmeiners played in Zappacosta, who sent an angled ball back across the box; Lookman, lurking behind two team-mates, finished from the far post. Sky Sports: Koopmeiners won the ball after a partially cleared corner and passed inside to Zappacosta, who pulled it back across the box; Lookman got behind Palacios and side-footed in. Agree on all three contacts.

goals.notes: Score is Atalanta's tally first, after the goal. UEFA (official): Lookman needed no help, wove to the edge of the box and hit a low effort past Kovar. Sky Sports: Leverkusen lost the ball in transition, Lookman collected it, played it through Xhaka's legs and curled a shot in from about 20 yards. The Xhaka nutmeg and the 20-yard distance are Sky-only details, kept in notes, not in the sequence.

goals.notes: Score is Atalanta's tally first, after the goal. UEFA (official analysis): cross from the right, Scamacca first-time right-foot finish. Sky Sports: Zappacosta low cross, Scamacca peeled off Konate and Van Dijk into a central position, first-time finish past Kelleher; minute 38. goals.notes: Score is Atalanta's tally first, after the goal. UEFA (official analysis): De Ketelaere slid wide and delivered a first-time cross from the right; Scamacca finished first time with his left foot. goals.notes: Score is Atalanta's tally first, after the goal. Sky Sports: Szoboszlai lost the ball in midfield, Ederson was freed, Kelleher's poor parry left the net open and Pasalic tapped in; text says 84, match header 83 (minute 83 used, header). Guardian/Irish Times: Szoboszlai's loose pass, Scamacca played in Ederson, whose first-time shot was saved, Pasalic converted the rebound. The freeing pass is named (Scamacca) only by the Guardian, so it is kept unnamed.
